title: a DF-005 reconciliation source — the task list, or the project's gap/gate records
description: AUTHORED by the project, or printed on stdout by a project adapter. This pack has no writer: it owns the INVOCATION and the OUTCOME SEMANTICS, never a project's native task format. Both sides of the comparison use this one shape, because the comparison is symmetric — DF-005 is drift in BOTH directions at once, and a schema that described only the task side would encode the half-implementation the finding is about. additionalProperties is TRUE at every level: a project's records carry its own fields, and the reconciler reads only the ones below.
$comment: ⛔ THE RECORD ARRAY'S LOCATION IS PROJECT-DECLARED (state.reconcile.*.pointer), so this schema cannot name the key that holds it. It does the next best thing rather than the vacuous thing: ANY array in this document must be an array of records. A first draft declared $defs/record and never referenced it, which validated nothing at all while reading like a specification — the exact failure the validator's refuse-what-you-cannot-enforce rule exists to prevent, one level up.

oneOf.title: the source IS the record array (no pointer declared)
the records sit under a project-declared pointer

schemaVersion.description: Optional — a source that declares none is read on its own terms. A source that declares one this kernel does not support is REFUSED by name (drift class UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION), never read on a best-effort basis.

record.description: The comparable record. Reachable at whatever `pointer` the project declares, which is why this is a $def rather than a fixed property — a project's task file may nest its rows anywhere.

id.description: The STABLE identifier both sides share. Without one there is nothing to reconcile, so a record with no string id is rejected and reported rather than skipped.

status.description: The project's own word. It is mapped to open/closed through openStatuses/closedStatuses. ⛔ An UNMAPPED word is not guessed: the record becomes undetermined and drags the verdict to CANNOT_DETERMINE, because guessing 'probably open' lets a typo silently close a gap.
